role: Incident Responder (Digital Forensics and Incident Response)

evidence.quote: I opened the ticket under the ransomware-precursor category. That staging-directory behavior is just what I've been seeing constantly lately, so it felt like the obvious bucket.
evidence.explanation: The worker forms a diagnostic model of the incident by generalising from prior cases, categorising an ambiguous technical event under an explanatory framework rather than merely retrieving a fact.

evidence.quote: I decided the 9-host signal was probably noise from that same original window and kept the scope close to 3.
evidence.explanation: The participant builds an explanatory model of what the new signal represents (noise vs. expansion), which requires abstraction beyond the raw data point.

evidence.quote: That's when it became clear the playbook's two options hadn't covered that angle at all.
evidence.explanation: The worker forms an understanding of a systemic gap in the response framework, a conceptual diagnosis rather than a simple lookup.

secondary_categories.subcategory: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation

evidence.quote: Around 1 a.m. I got a SIEM alert for an off-hours process spawning a staging directory on the finance file server... There was also a quieter log line underneath it.
evidence.explanation: The worker gathers and evaluates competing log/alert evidence from a security monitoring system as a core part of triage.

evidence.quote: About 40 minutes later, an EDR sweep came back showing authentication artifacts touching 9 more hosts — lower confidence, but there.
evidence.explanation: The worker retrieves and evaluates the reliability of additional evidence from an EDR tool before deciding on scope.

evidence.quote: I ran my own PowerShell isolation and log-collection script — I wrote that thing two years ago
evidence.explanation: Authoring and applying a custom script to solve a nonstandard containment problem reflects a self-generated technical solution, not a purely routine act.

evidence.quote: There's an escalation path to our external IR retainer that could've given a broader set of options
evidence.explanation: Weighing whether to pursue a non-default escalation route to expand the option set is a planning-type resolution activity, even though it was ultimately not exercised.

evidence.quote: Within the first ten minutes I set the ticket scope at 3 endpoints... showing authentication artifacts touching 9 more hosts
evidence.explanation: The worker tracks, compares, and reasons about specific numeric host counts and time intervals (10 minutes, 40 minutes, 3 vs. 9 vs. 7 hosts) to determine incident scope.

evidence.quote: the finance director started pinging for an update ahead of the 6 a.m. close deadline, so there was real pressure to say something concrete... I'd already told the director "3 hosts, contained"
evidence.explanation: The worker manages a stakeholder relationship and communicates a status commitment that has operational consequences, aligning with coordinating across organisational actors during an incident.

A1.3 Navigation - no physical movement through space described (work is remote/overnight, over chat and systems)
A3.1 Serving and attending - the interaction with the director is a reporting obligation, not a service-attending relationship
A3.2 Teaching, training, and coaching - no instructional activity present
A3.3 Selling and influencing - the lead's suggestion is received, not the participant persuading another party
A3.5 Caring - no welfare or personal care activity present
ambiguities: The lead's recommendation to use EDR isolation could be read as light coordination/teamwork (A3.4) or as an external input to an individual intellectual decision; classified here primarily as intellectual tool-selection reasoning by the participant, with the social coordination aspect noted only for the director-update episode where an explicit commitment and expectation-management exchange is described.

evidence.quote: So triage, scoping, containment, remediation — all of it was on me until morning.
evidence.explanation: The participant held sole decision authority overnight across the entire incident lifecycle, indicating high discretion over sequencing and method.

evidence.quote: So I kept running my script across the hosts, and only tried the EDR isolation on a couple of them after my lead brought it up a second time.
evidence.explanation: The worker retained discretion to choose a containment method even against a colleague's suggestion.

evidence.quote: The ticketing system's playbook for that category gave me exactly two actions: reset affected credentials, and reimage the affected endpoints.
evidence.explanation: Remediation choices were structured and constrained by a predefined playbook, indicating procedural control, though the worker retained discretion in categorisation and tool choice.

evidence.quote: Two days later, compliance asked whether we'd preserved a forensic image of the staging directory before reimaging
evidence.explanation: A compliance function later reviewed and questioned the actions taken, indicating post-hoc monitoring/audit of the work.

evidence.quote: My senior lead was reachable on chat but not really available to jump on calls.
evidence.explanation: The worker operated largely solo overnight, with only asynchronous, limited-bandwidth contact with a colleague, indicating low direct collaborative dependence during the episode.

evidence.quote: I'd closed six tickets in the past three weeks that all started exactly like this, staging directory, off-hours process
evidence.explanation: The initial alert pattern recurs frequently in the worker's recent caseload, indicating a repetitive input type, even though the specific incident's handling diverged from the routine pattern.

evidence.quote: The ticketing system's playbook for that category gave me exactly two actions
evidence.explanation: Remediation follows a prescribed playbook tied to an incident category, indicating standardised procedure, though scoping and containment left room for individual method choice.

evidence.quote: no ransom note, no encryption, no mass renaming, so nothing screaming "this is it" yet.
evidence.explanation: The available signals were ambiguous and did not conclusively indicate the nature of the incident, reflecting low certainty about inputs and consequences.

evidence.quote: an EDR sweep came back showing authentication artifacts touching 9 more hosts — lower confidence, but there.
evidence.explanation: Explicit low-confidence data further supports low certainty in the operating environment.

evidence.quote: compliance asked whether we'd preserved a forensic image of the staging directory before reimaging, since that affects whether this gets reported as a data exposure.
evidence.explanation: The worker had to respond to an incident whose full implications (compliance/legal exposure) emerged only after initial action, requiring handling of unanticipated developments.

evidence.quote: It wasn't built for a scope that size, honestly, it's more of a one-or-two-host tool.
evidence.explanation: The tool available was not designed for the scale encountered, requiring the worker to adapt to an unexpected situation.
